title: The Real Reason Early Wi‑Fi Failed

scenes.text: Why the 1997 Linksys router barely reached a room

scenes.label: UNLICENSED 2.4 GHZ BAND
scenes.text: It used the unregulated 2.4 GHz band, causing heavy interference from cordless phones and microwaves.

scenes.label: ANTENNA DESIGN LIMITS
scenes.text: The built‑in antenna was short and non‑directional, limiting signal strength.

scenes.label: NO MESH SUPPORT
scenes.text: Without mesh networking, each unit acted alone, leaving dead zones in larger homes.
Follow for the future, one byte at a time.

description: Learn the technical flaws that kept the first consumer Wi‑Fi routers confined to a single room. Stay tuned for more tech breakdowns.
